advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Make list_processes() assert `ps` actually ran: check proc.returncode (or raise on nonzero) and treat empty stdout as an error rather than 'no orphans', so a ps failure is distinguishable from a clean scan.
evidence: scripts/check_orphaned_load.py:135: `proc = subprocess.run(["ps", "-A", "-o", _PS_FORMAT], capture_output=True, text=True, check=False, timeout=_PS_TIMEOUT_SECONDS,)`
scripts/check_orphaned_load.py:144: `for line in proc.stdout.splitlines():` — proc.returncode is never read
scripts/check_orphaned_load.py:204: `if not flagged: return 0` — empty result maps to exit 0 whether ps ran or not

Litmus: name every world producing the exit-0 verdict — 'ps ran and found no orphans', 'ps exited nonzero', 'ps produced no stdout'. The check cannot distinguish its clean verdict from its own failure.
advisory.finding: list_processes() runs `ps` with check=False and never inspects proc.returncode; if ps exits nonzero, is absent, or emits nothing to stdout, the loop over proc.stdout.splitlines() yields zero records, find_orphaned_load returns [], and main() returns 0 — a 'clean' verdict indistinguishable from ps having failed or never produced output.
scenarios: `ps` binary missing / PATH issue on a constrained host — nonzero exit, empty stdout, exit 0 reported as clean
`ps` writes an error to stderr and nothing to stdout — detector silently reports clean while orphans persist
advisory.suggested_fix: After subprocess.run, raise (or exit nonzero with a distinct message) when proc.returncode != 0 or proc.stdout is empty, since the live process table is never legitimately empty (the smoke test itself asserts `records` is non-empty).

advisory.finding: _parse_ps_line() catches ValueError and returns None, silently discarding any row whose pid/ppid/time fails to parse; combined with the un-checked ps invocation, systematic parse failure (e.g. a locale/format change in `time=`) drops rows invisibly and can produce an all-clear with no diagnostic.
scenarios: A ps TIME format the parser doesn't recognize on some platform makes every hot row unparseable, yielding an empty flagged set and exit 0
